name: Rice (Paddy)
description: The world's most widely consumed staple cereal, grown in flooded fields with heavy water demand; India is the largest producer. Strong year-round demand and government procurement make it the anchor crop of most rice-belt farms.

agronomy.land_prep: Puddling in standing water; level field
agronomy.irrigation: Continuous flooding 2–5 cm during vegetative stage

pests.name: Brown plant hopper
pests.treatment: Imidacloprid spray; drain field before application

pests.name: Blast disease
pests.treatment: Tricyclazole or carbendazim at first signs

name: Wheat
description: The principal winter (rabi) cereal of the Indo-Gangetic plains, sown in cool dry weather and irrigated at critical growth stages. Strong procurement at minimum support price keeps the market dependable for growers.

agronomy.irrigation: 5–6 critical-stage irrigations (CRI, tillering, flowering)

pests.name: Rust (yellow/stem)
pests.treatment: Propiconazole at first pustules; resistant varieties

name: Maize (Corn)
description: A versatile, fast-growing cereal used for human food, poultry and cattle feed, starch and ethanol industries. Its short season and wide climate tolerance make it a reliable kharif option for rainfed and irrigated farms alike.

agronomy.land_prep: Deep ploughing to 20–25 cm; break clods
agronomy.irrigation: Every 7–10 days; critical at tasseling and grain filling

pests.name: Fall armyworm
pests.treatment: Emamectin benzoate; pheromone traps; early planting

name: Sorghum (Jowar)
description: Drought-tolerant cereal that thrives on low rainfall and poor soils, used for flatbreads (jowar roti), animal feed, and fodder. Its resilience makes it a lifeline in semi-arid regions and a rising export grain.

agronomy.irrigation: Mostly rainfed; 2–3 protective irrigations if dry

pests.name: Grain mold
pests.treatment: Harvest early; dry grain below 12% moisture

name: Pearl Millet (Bajra)
description: The most drought-hardy staple cereal, grown on sandy soils of hot arid regions with minimal water. Its grains are rich in iron and zinc, and growing health-food demand plus MSP procurement support prices.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; 1–2 lifesaving irrigations in long dry spells
agronomy.intercropping: Pigeon pea, green gram, cluster bean

name: Finger Millet (Ragi)
description: A calcium-rich millet that stores exceptionally well for months, making it a food-security crop in hills and dry regions. Rising demand for gluten-free, nutritious grains is steadily lifting its market value.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; irrigate at tillering and earhead emergence if dry

name: Barley (Jau)
description: A short-duration, salt-tolerant winter cereal used for animal feed, malt and beer, and health foods. It suits marginal and saline soils where wheat struggles, with dependable malt-industry buyers.

overview.soil_type: Loam to sandy loam; tolerates salinity

agronomy.irrigation: 2–3 irrigations; avoid excess at maturity

name: Oats
description: A cool-season cereal grown for nutritious grain, breakfast foods, and as a high-quality green fodder cut multiple times. Health-food demand for oats keeps prices firm in urban markets.

agronomy.irrigation: 3–4 irrigations in dry winters

name: Chickpea (Chana)
description: India's most important pulse, grown on residual moisture after the monsoon; its nitrogen-fixing roots rebuild soil fertility. Strong dal demand and government procurement make it one of the most profitable rabi pulses.

agronomy.land_prep: Zero/minimum tillage after paddy or deep ploughing
agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; one irrigation at pod filling if available

pests.name: Wilt
pests.treatment: Resistant varieties; seed treatment with Trichoderma

name: Pigeon Pea (Arhar)
description: A deep-rooted, drought-tolerant pulse grown as a kharif-to-rabi crop, widely intercropped with cereals; the standing crop also provides green fodder and firewood. Arhar dal commands premium prices due to perennial domestic shortage.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; critical at flowering and pod development

pests.name: Wilt
pests.treatment: Resistant varieties; seed dressing with Trichoderma

name: Green Gram (Moong)
description: A short-duration, heat-tolerant pulse that fits into every cropping gap — as a catch crop, rotation crop, or green manure; its roots fix nitrogen for the following crop. Quick returns and firm dal prices make it a farmer favourite.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; one irrigation at flowering if dry

name: Black Gram (Urad)
description: A premium pulse whose white-split form (urad dal) is essential in Indian kitchens; it thrives on heavy soils and fixes nitrogen. Persistent supply gaps keep wholesale prices among the highest of the pulses.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; 1–2 irrigations in dry spells

name: Lentil (Masoor)
description: A cool-season pulse grown on residual moisture, valued for its quick cooking and high protein; its straw is good animal feed. Steady demand in vegetarian markets and short duration make it a dependable rabi rotation crop.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; one irrigation at flowering if possible

name: Cowpea (Lobia)
description: An extremely heat- and drought-tolerant legume used for grain, green pods as a vegetable, and fodder; it improves soil nitrogen in dryland rotations. A staple protein source in much of Africa with reliable regional demand.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; 1–2 irrigations if prolonged dry spell

name: Groundnut
description: A nitrogen-fixing oilseed and confectionery crop whose pods mature underground; it also improves soil for the next crop. Edible-oil demand, peanut butter processing, and export markets give it diversified buyers.

agronomy.land_prep: Deep ploughing; raised bed / ridge planting
agronomy.irrigation: Critical at pegging and pod development

name: Soybean
description: The world's leading oilseed and protein crop, crushed for edible oil with the de-oiled cake used in poultry and cattle feed. Strong crushing-industry demand in central India makes it a major kharif cash rotation.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; critical at flowering and pod filling

name: Mustard (Sarson)
description: India's primary winter oilseed, with bright yellow flowers and seed crushed into cooking oil; the de-oiled cake feeds livestock. Its short season fits perfectly between kharif harvest and summer, with MSP support each year.

agronomy.irrigation: 2–3 irrigations: flowering and siliqua filling

name: Sesame (Til)
description: A heat-tolerant oilseed with premium golden oil and a large export market for seeds and tahini; it matures quickly on light soils. High per-quintal prices reward careful harvest and drying.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; 1–2 lifesaving irrigations

name: Sunflower
description: A short-duration oilseed with light, healthy oil and bee-attracting flowers that aid pollination of nearby crops. Its quick maturity suits multiple sowing windows, though yields demand good management.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and seed filling

name: Castor
description: An industrial oilseed whose non-edible oil feeds lubricants, paints, and cosmetics; India is the world's leading producer and exporter. Contract buying and export demand give it stable, often high, returns on marginal land.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; critical at flowering and capsule set

name: Linseed (Flax)
description: A dual-purpose winter crop yielding omega-3-rich seeds (flaxseed) for health foods and oil, plus fiber for textiles. Rising superfood demand is expanding its market beyond traditional oilseed buyers.

agronomy.irrigation: 2–3 irrigations in dry winters

name: Tomato
description: The highest-value vegetable in most markets, grown year-round under irrigation with staking and regular pest scouting. Demand from fresh retail, processing (paste, ketchup), and exports gives growers multiple sale channels.

agronomy.land_prep: Deep ploughing with organic matter; raised beds
agronomy.irrigation: Drip irrigation preferred; avoid moisture swings

name: Onion
description: A high-value bulb crop with year-round kitchen demand and export markets; proper curing and storage let growers sell into price peaks. Price volatility is the main risk, rewarded by strong returns in lean seasons.

agronomy.irrigation: Light, frequent — every 3–5 days

name: Potato
description: The fourth most important food crop worldwide, grown from seed tubers in cool weather; processing units (chips, fries) offer contracted buyers. Cold storage allows farmers to hold stock and sell at better winter prices.

agronomy.irrigation: Every 7–10 days; critical at tuber initiation

name: Garlic
description: A high-value bulb crop with huge culinary and medicinal demand; cloves are planted in cool weather and bulbs cured after harvest. Prices are among the best of any vegetable when supply tightens.

agronomy.irrigation: 5–6 irrigations; stop before harvest

name: Okra (Bhindi)
description: A warm-season vegetable harvested continuously over 2–3 months, giving farmers multiple income flushes from one planting. Fresh market, export, and processing (frozen, dehydrated) all absorb production.

agronomy.irrigation: Every 5–7 days; critical at flowering

name: Brinjal (Eggplant)
description: A long-harvesting vegetable with many regional varieties, rich in fiber and antioxidants; plants fruit for months, spreading income. Steady everyday demand makes it a staple of peri-urban vegetable farms.

agronomy.irrigation: Drip or furrow every 4–7 days

name: Cauliflower
description: A cool-season cole crop whose curd forms poorly in heat or frost, so variety choice and timing are critical. Wholesale, retail, and processing (frozen) channels give consistent demand through winter.

agronomy.irrigation: Every 5–7 days; avoid stress during curd formation

pests.name: Black rot
pests.treatment: Resistant varieties; copper spray; crop rotation

name: Cabbage
description: A hardy, heavy-yielding cole crop that grows in cool weather and stores well; it is a cheap everyday vegetable with steady retail demand. Good head quality and timely harvest protect margins.

agronomy.irrigation: Every 4–6 days; head formation critical

name: Carrot
description: A beta-carotene-rich root vegetable of cool winters; loose, stone-free soil is essential for straight roots. Salad, juice, and processing demand keep it a reliable rabi vegetable for local markets.

agronomy.irrigation: Light and frequent; avoid crusting

name: Green Peas
description: A cool-season vegetable legume harvested as green pods; nitrogen-fixing roots also enrich the soil for the next crop. Frozen-pea processors contract early-season volumes, steadying prices.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and pod filling

resources.title: Peas for Fresh and Frozen Markets

name: Capsicum (Bell Pepper)
description: A colorful, vitamin-rich vegetable grown for fresh retail and processing; colored varieties (yellow, red) command premium prices. Staking, pruning, and steady irrigation protect quality and returns.

agronomy.irrigation: Drip every 2–3 days

name: Chili Pepper
description: A high-value spice crop dried and sold for culinary, oleoresin, and dye extraction; India is the world's largest producer and exporter. Quality drying and grading unlock the best export prices.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and fruit set

name: Cucumber
description: A quick-maturing, high-water-content summer vegetable harvested within two months of sowing. Frequent picking over several weeks and fresh retail demand make it a fast cash crop for small farms.

agronomy.land_prep: Raised beds / ridges; trellis for quality
agronomy.irrigation: Frequent; avoid water stress at fruiting

name: Bitter Gourd (Karela)
description: A medicinally valued gourd whose bitter fruits are a kitchen staple and increasingly sought for juice and nutraceuticals. Trellising and regular picking over 2–3 months keep income flowing.

agronomy.irrigation: Every 3–5 days; mulching conserves water

name: Bottle Gourd (Lauki)
description: A high-yielding climbing gourd grown for its tender fruits, widely used in curries and juice; young fruits are picked repeatedly. Its bulk and moderate price suit farmers targeting steady local markets.

agronomy.irrigation: Regular; mulching helps

name: Ridge Gourd (Turai)
description: A fast-growing ridge-climbing gourd harvested young, with steady everyday demand in vegetable markets. Multiple pickings over weeks make it a dependable cash crop for summer gardens.

agronomy.irrigation: Every 3–5 days

name: Pumpkin
description: A sprawling vining vegetable whose mature fruits store for months without cold storage, letting farmers sell into off-season price rises. Culinary, seed, and processing (puree) markets all exist.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and fruit growth

name: Sweet Potato
description: A nutritious, drought-tolerant tuber crop propagated from vine cuttings, rich in beta-carotene; it yields well on light soils with little input. Growing demand for healthy staples supports firm prices.

agronomy.land_prep: Ridges and furrows; light soil preferred
agronomy.irrigation: Critical at vine establishment and tuber bulking

name: Yam
region: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, UP + West Africa
description: A starchy tuber that is a staple in West Africa and South India, grown from small tuber setts with staking; it stores well for many months. Strong regional and diaspora demand keeps prices firm.

agronomy.irrigation: Regular; mulching for moisture

name: Turmeric (Haldi)
description: The golden spice with booming demand from cooking, cosmetics, and curcumin health supplements; rhizomes are boiled, dried, and polished before sale. India dominates world production and export.

agronomy.irrigation: Regular until maturity; reduce before harvest

name: Ginger
description: An aromatic rhizome used fresh, dried, and in beverages and medicines, with strong export demand; it needs shade, moisture, and loose soil. High per-kg prices reward careful rhizome selection and disease control.

agronomy.irrigation: Light and frequent; avoid waterlogging

name: Cardamom (Elaichi)
description: The 'Queen of Spices' — a shade-loving highland perennial whose green pods are among the world's most valuable spices per kilo. Long investment horizon, but plantation yields pay exceptionally well.

agronomy.irrigation: Drip/misting in dry months

name: Black Pepper
description: The 'King of Spices' — a perennial vine trained on support trees or live standards, bearing spikes of peppercorns sun-dried to black. Premium export prices reward quality curing and vine health.

agronomy.irrigation: Mulch + irrigation in dry months

name: Coriander (Dhania)
description: A dual-purpose spice grown for fresh leafy greens (cilantro) and dried seeds used in every Indian spice blend; it matures quickly. Leaf harvests bring fast cash while seed crops target spice markets.

agronomy.land_prep: Fine tilth; light irrigation after sowing
agronomy.irrigation: Light and frequent; avoid excess at flowering

name: Cumin (Jeera)
description: A small-seeded, cool-dry spice with indispensable culinary demand and high export value; India is the world's largest producer. Prices can spike sharply in short-supply years, rewarding well-timed sales.

agronomy.irrigation: 2–3 irrigations; stop before harvest

name: Sugarcane
description: A long-duration cash crop with assured mill procurement at fair remunerative prices; ratoon management extends productivity without replanting. Heavy water and fertilizer use reward attentive growers.

agronomy.irrigation: Heavy; formative and grand growth critical

pests.name: Red rot
pests.treatment: Resistant varieties + sett treatment with carbendazim

name: Cotton
description: The world's most important fiber crop, with strong domestic mill and export demand; Bt hybrids have cut bollworm losses. Long duration and price volatility make it a high-stakes but proven cash rotation.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at squaring, flowering, boll development

pests.name: Bollworm complex
pests.treatment: Bt hybrids + IPM; chlorantraniliprole if needed

name: Tea
description: A plantation crop of cool, humid hills where tender shoots are plucked every 7–10 days for over 40 years; India is the world's second-largest producer. Consistent domestic consumption and export demand underpin prices.

agronomy.land_prep: Terracing on slopes; shade tree planting
agronomy.irrigation: Sprinkler/mist in dry months

name: Coffee
description: A premium shade-grown plantation crop of the Western Ghats, with India's arabica fetching strong export premiums. Specialty and sustainability-certified lots are increasingly sold directly to roasters at higher prices.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and berry filling

name: Rubber
description: A long-lived plantation tree tapped for latex used in tires and industrial goods; trees yield for 25+ years once mature. Stable industrial demand and rising tyre-sector consumption support prices.

agronomy.irrigation: Mulching; rainfed mostly

name: Tobacco
description: A high-value leaf crop grown under auction-board regulation in India, with export and domestic cigarette demand; curing and grading determine price. Regulated auctions provide a structured, transparent market.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical after transplant and at topping

name: Jute
description: The 'golden fiber', an eco-friendly bast fiber retted from stems for sacks, yarn, and increasingly geotextiles; it thrives in the humid Gangetic delta. Growing bans on plastics are expanding jute-based packaging demand.

agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; avoid water stress at vegetative peak

name: Mango
description: The 'King of Fruits' and India's national fruit; India is the world's largest producer, exporting fresh and processed (pulp, juice) mango. Mature orchards yield for decades with strong domestic and export demand.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering, fruit set, and development

pests.name: Mango weevil
pests.treatment: Clean orchard floor; post-harvest hot water

name: Banana
description: The world's most consumed fruit, grown from suckers with ratoon cropping giving year-round income; India is the largest producer. Fresh fruit, ripening chambers, and processing all absorb production.

agronomy.irrigation: Drip daily in summer; critical at flowering

name: Grapes
description: A premium trellised fruit with export-grade table varieties (Thompson Seedless) and wine grapes; India exports table grapes to Europe and Asia. High management intensity is rewarded with top-tier prices.

agronomy.irrigation: Drip; critical at berry development

name: Orange
description: A vitamin-C-rich citrus with year-round demand for fresh fruit and juice; Nagpur mandarins are India's most famous orange. Good orchard sanitation and irrigation timing drive quality and price.

agronomy.land_prep: Pits with FYM; grafted plants on rootstock
agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and fruit development

name: Papaya
description: A fast-bearing fruit tree that starts fruiting within a year of planting; papain extraction from unripe fruit adds an industrial income stream. Quick returns make it popular on small and medium farms.

agronomy.land_prep: Pits with FYM; good drainage essential
agronomy.irrigation: Regular; mulching recommended

name: Guava
description: A hardy, high-yielding fruit tree rich in Vitamin C, bearing fruit nearly year-round with low management needs; it tolerates poor soils and drought. Fresh and processing (juice, jelly) markets are steady.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and fruit set

name: Pomegranate
description: A drought-tolerant fruit with premium aril (seed) demand for fresh retail, juice, and exports to Europe and the Gulf. Its high water-use efficiency suits dry regions where other fruits struggle.

agronomy.irrigation: Drip; regulated deficit before flowering

name: Watermelon
description: A quick, high-water-content summer fruit that matures in under three months on sandy soils; it needs abundant irrigation and good pollination. Fast cycles and strong seasonal demand reward early-market growers.

agronomy.irrigation: High; critical at flowering and fruit growth

name: Apple
description: The premier temperate fruit of Himalayan valleys, needing winter chilling and careful orchard management; high-density plantings on dwarf rootstocks are raising yields. Premium table grades and processing both pay well.

agronomy.irrigation: Drip; critical at flowering and fruit sizing

name: Lemon
description: A versatile citrus with year-round fruit production in two main flushes, essential for cooking, beverages, and juice concentrate; it bears almost continuously in warm climates. Steady all-season demand keeps prices firm.

agronomy.irrigation: Critical at flowering and fruit development

name: Sisal
description: A rugged, drought-hardy agave yielding strong white fiber for ropes, carpets, and composites, thriving on poor dry soils with minimal care; East Africa is a major producing region. Leaves are cut for 7–10 years per plant.

agronomy.land_prep: Light land preparation; contour planting on slopes
agronomy.irrigation: Rainfed; drought tolerant
